gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-005 diagnoses an invalid equality-to-full-stationarity inference caused by a projection kernel. It does not diagnose the undefined Fourier phase or the incorrect spatial-component fallback in the revised exit-wave definition.

ISSUE-004 concerns an erroneous coarse/fine-grid reciprocal averaging identity. It does not identify the separate failure that arbitrary u can make the PIE quadratic nonpositive, cause division by zero, or eliminate existence of the minimizer.

ISSUE-005 addresses the projection-kernel failure in an equality characterization. It does not recognize the distinct defect in testing whether a Fourier phase equals zero, nor the resulting invalid or altered phase-recycling construction.

Both identify the false converse in the theorem's biconditional: stationarity of the new iterate does not imply equality of consecutive objective values. ISSUE-001 supplies the matching scalar counterexample and the supported one-way repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The theorem incorrectly asserts equivalence between equality of consecutive objective values and stationarity of the new iterate; only equality implying stationarity is established.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed converse from stationarity of the new iterate to equality of consecutive objective values is false, while only the reverse implication is supported.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly identifies the unsupported converse, demonstrates it with the same scalar setup and strict-decrease counterexample, and proposes replacing the biconditional by the valid one-way implication.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that equality in the projected descent expression implies only vanishing projected/coarse gradient, not vanishing fine-grid gradient, because the restriction has a nontrivial kernel. ISSUE-005 gives the matching kernel example and corrected restricted-stationarity statement.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The equality case of the descent inner product certifies only restricted stationarity I_h^H grad=0; it cannot certify full fine-grid stationarity because the restriction operator has a nontrivial kernel.

component_coverage.gold_component: The asserted equality-to-full-stationarity conclusion is invalid because projected-gradient zero does not imply full-gradient zero; only restricted stationarity follows.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the projected quadratic vanishes when the coarse projection of the gradient vanishes, gives a nonzero fine-grid gradient in the projection kernel, and correctly weakens the conclusion to projected stationarity.
